result.summary:
Implemented docs/agents/design/REQ-025.md (CODE-DESIGNER) + docs/agents/design/REQ-025-schema.md (DATA-DESIGNER) exactly as designed.

1. apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts: NEW `notificationLedger` table per REQ-025-schema.md §4 -- id (UUID PK), registration_id (UUID NOT NULL FK -> registrations.id, ON DELETE RESTRICT), kind (text, app-validated), created_at/updated_at (timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()), and the load-bearing `UNIQUE(registration_id, kind)` index (uq_notification_ledger_registration_kind). Migration generated via `drizzle-kit generate` in apps/bot (never hand-written): apps/bot/drizzle/0005_violet_venom.sql contains exactly one CREATE TABLE + one FK ALTER + one CREATE UNIQUE INDEX, matching the schema doc's own predicted SQL (§5) statement-for-statement.

2. apps/bot/src/domain/notification.ts (NEW): framework-free (decisions/0004, no grammy import) per design §2/§3. `NotificationKind` (6-member union), `SendClassification` (2-member union, AC5 satisfied structurally -- `SendNotificationInput.classification` has no `?` and no default anywhere), `NotificationSender` interface, `SendNotificationInput`, `SendOutcome`, and `sendLedgeredNotification` implementing §3.1's ordered rule table literally: step1 user lookup (skipped-no-telegram-id), step2 unconditional blocked check before the classification branch (AC4), step3 marketing-only broadcastOptIn check, never read for transactional (AC3), step4 the single atomic ledger INSERT with Postgres 23505 (unique-violation) caught and converted to skipped-already-sent -- unwraps one level through drizzle-orm's DrizzleQueryError wrapper to find the underlying pg error's `.code` (a real bug caught and fixed during AC1 verification, see issues below) -- step5 composeMessage + sender.send, ledger row never rolled back on send failure (§3.2's accepted under-sending risk). Never throws; every branch returns a SendOutcome.

3. apps/bot/src/scheduler/rateLimiter.ts (NEW): imports grammy (the one place NotificationSender's interface is implemented), per design §5. `RateLimiterConfig`, `DEFAULT_RATE_LIMITER_CONFIG` (maxMessagesPerSecond:25, maxRetries:5, initialBackoffMs:1000, maxBackoffMs:30000 -- the design's exact fixed numbers), `createRateLimitedSender(bot, config)`. A rolling one-second-window pacer (proactive pacing, never drops/errors, waits for a free slot) and `sendWithRetry` implementing the 429 rule table exactly: `GrammyError.error_code === 429` detection, waits `parameters.retry_after` seconds (or initialBackoffMs if absent), retries the SAME logical send, doubles the wait each successive 429 up to maxBackoffMs, up to maxRetries total attempts; a non-429 error propagates immediately, unretried; exhaustion after maxRetries throws (converted by sendLedgeredNotification's step 5 catch into `{kind:'failed', error}`, never an uncaught throw past that boundary).

4. apps/bot/src/scheduler/runner.ts (NEW): framework-free per design §7. `ScheduledJobDefinition`, `SchedulerHandle`, `startScheduledJobs(jobs)` -- one setInterval per job, an immediate first run (restart catch-up), a per-job running-flag overlap guard (skip, not queue, not concurrent), failure isolation (a rejected run is caught and logged via log.ts's createLogger, never crashes the process or stops other jobs' timers), `stop()` clearing every timer. One deliberate, disclosed deviation from the design's literal one-argument signature: since the design's own text says failures are logged 'via this codebase's existing log.ts logger' but the stated signature takes no logger parameter, this module constructs its own logger internally (`createLogger('debug')`) rather than adding an undesigned second parameter -- safe because log.ts's LEVEL_ORDER makes `.error()` fire regardless of which threshold is passed (error is LEVEL_ORDER's own maximum). Flagged as an issue below for REVIEWER to confirm or override.

5. apps/bot/src/domain/user.ts: `UserForNotification` gains `broadcastOptIn: boolean` (REQ-025.md §6); `getUserForNotificationById`'s query gains the one additional selected column `broadcastOptIn: users.broadcastOptIn` (no schema change -- REQ-010's existing column).

6. apps/bot/src/handlers/withdraw.ts: `sendPromotionNotification` rewritten per design §4 exactly -- `ctx: Context` parameter removed, replaced by an injected `sender: NotificationSender`; parameter renamed `withdrawnRegistrationId` -> `promotedRegistrationId`; the function body's own guard/compose logic (blocked check, null-tgId guard, language resolution) is now entirely delegated to `sendLedgeredNotification`'s own steps -- this function is a thin `composeMessage` closure (the exact same [admittedPrefix, eventTitle, dateTimeText, qrLabel+qrToken, whatNext] text, unchanged, per the content-shape note) plus one `sendLedgeredNotification({..., kind:'waitlist_promotion', classification:'transactional', registrationId: promotedRegistrationId, ...})` call. `makeWithdrawConfirmCallbackHandler(db, sender)` gains the second parameter; its one internal call site now passes `outcome.promotion.registrationId` (the PROMOTED row's own id, not the withdrawn row's) per design §4 point 2.

7. apps/bot/src/index.ts: constructs the one process-wide `notificationSender` via `createRateLimitedSender(bot, DEFAULT_RATE_LIMITER_CONFIG)`, calls `startScheduledJobs([])` (an empty job list -- REQ-025 ships the runner mechanism only, no concrete reminder job, per design §7's own scope note), and passes `notificationSender` into `makeWithdrawConfirmCallbackHandler(db, notificationSender)`.

8. Test-file updates (not new committed test files for REQ-025 itself -- its own ACs are two-genuine-process/real-429-stub scenarios verified via scratch harness scripts, written, run, then deleted, per REQ-019's own established precedent for this class of AC): apps/bot/src/handlers/withdraw.test.ts and apps/bot/src/handlers/my.test.ts updated to construct a real `createRateLimitedSender` and pass it as makeWithdrawConfirmCallbackHandler's new second argument, so the existing REQ-022/023/024 suites keep passing unchanged through the new ledger-backed send path.

All 6 ACs verified with real output against a live scratch Postgres (apps/bot/docker-compose.yml, port 55432, freshly migrated via `drizzle-kit migrate` including the new 0005 migration) -- see evidence.commands and ac_results below. REQ-023's own existing promotion-notification tests (withdraw.test.ts, both the broadcast_opt_in=false transactional-send case and the S10 blocked-user-skip case) were re-run and still pass unchanged, confirming the withdraw.ts migration onto the ledger did not regress anything.

Commands run from the REPO ROOT: `npm run lint --workspace=apps/bot` -> exit 0, 0 errors. `npm run build --workspace=apps/bot` -> exit 0, tsc clean. `TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://bot:bot@localhost:55432/bot npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism` (repo root, no path filter) -> 19 files / 217 tests passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped -- identical count to REQ-024's own confirmed baseline (217), because REQ-025 adds no new committed vitest test file (its own ACs are two-process/stubbed-429 scenarios outside vitest's process model, per the design's own AC1 instruction that a single-run/single-process test is not evidence). `git status --porcelain` confirms only apps/bot/src/db/schema.ts, apps/bot/src/domain/user.ts, apps/bot/src/handlers/{withdraw.ts,withdraw.test.ts,my.test.ts}, apps/bot/src/index.ts, apps/bot/drizzle/{0005_violet_venom.sql,meta/*} modified/added, plus the two new files apps/bot/src/domain/notification.ts and apps/bot/src/scheduler/{rateLimiter.ts,runner.ts} -- nothing outside apps/bot/** touched; no scratch-verify-*.ts file left behind (all deleted after use, per this run's own discipline).

REFERENCES registrations(id) ON DELETE restrict, one CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_notification_ledger_registration_kind ON (registration_id, kind)) -- diffed directly against REQ-025-schema.md §5's predicted SQL, statement-for-statement match
cd apps/bot && docker compose up -d -> bot-postgres-1 started fresh; DATABASE_URL=postgres://bot:bot@localhost:55432/bot npm run migrate -> migrations applied successfully (0001-0005)
npm run build --workspace=apps/bot -> exit 0, tsc clean
TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://bot:bot@localhost:55432/bot npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism (repo root, full suite) -> 19 files / 217 tests passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped

TEST_DATABASE_URL=... npx vitest run apps/bot/src/handlers/withdraw.test.ts --reporter=verbose -> 6/6 passed individually, including 'REQ-023 AC6: the promoted person is notified even with broadcast_opt_in=false' and 'S10 rework: a blocked promoted person's promotion completes with no notification sent' -- both exercising sendPromotionNotification's NEW ledger-backed call path

AC1 (genuine two-process kill+restart, apps/bot/scratch-verify-req025-ac1-phase1.ts + -phase2.ts, deleted after use): phase 1 run via `npx tsx` in the background, seeded a fixture registration, called sendLedgeredNotification(kind:'reminder_24h') to completion (outcome {kind:'sent'}, 1 row in a scratch delivery-log table, 1 notification_ledger row), then printed PROCESS_READY_TO_KILL pid=16872 and hung on an unresolved Promise plus a keep-alive setInterval (added specifically so the process only ever exits via a genuine external kill signal, never pg's own idle-connection timeout -- an initial dry run without this keep-alive was observed to exit naturally after ~idle timeout before a kill signal could be sent, so the keep-alive was added and the run redone). Confirmed alive via `tasklist /FI "PID eq 16872"` (150MB RSS), then force-killed via `taskkill /PID 16872 /F` -> 'SUCCESS: the process ... has been terminated', re-confirmed via tasklist (no matching process). Read back via psql immediately after the kill: scratch_deliveries count=1, notification_ledger count=1. Phase 2, a wholly separate `npx tsx` invocation with no import of or reference to phase 1, re-derived the registration id purely from Postgres and re-ran the identical sendLedgeredNotification call -> outcome {kind:'skipped-already-sent'}, delivery count still 1, ledger row count still 1 -- exactly one message delivered across the full two-process restart

AC2 (apps/bot, ad hoc): `grep -rnE "new Set\(|new Map\(" src/` finds two matches, both unrelated to notifications (profile.ts's FREE_TEXT field-name sets, log.ts's REDACTED_KEYS set) -- zero in-memory idempotency tracker of any kind anywhere in domain/notification.ts, scheduler/*.ts, or handlers/withdraw.ts. Direct duplicate insert via psql: `INSERT INTO notification_ledger (registration_id, kind) VALUES ('<existing row's registration_id>', 'reminder_24h')` -> `ERROR: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "uq_notification_ledger_registration_kind"` -- confirms the DB-level UNIQUE constraint, not an in-memory record, is the sole idempotency mechanism

AC3/AC4 (apps/bot/scratch-verify-req025-ac3-ac4.ts, deleted after use): a broadcast_opt_in=false, non-blocked user -> transactional send outcome {kind:'sent'} (1 delivery), marketing send on the SAME user outcome {kind:'skipped-no-broadcast-opt-in'} (0 additional deliveries) -- both branches run against the same fixture, per AC3's own wording. A blocked=true, broadcast_opt_in=true user -> BOTH transactional and marketing calls return {kind:'skipped-blocked'}, 0 total deliveries -- AC4's 'neither send type' confirmed

AC5 (direct read): `grep -n classification apps/bot/src/domain/notification.ts` shows `classification: SendClassification;` inside SendNotificationInput -- no `?`, no default value anywhere in the file

AC6 (apps/bot/scratch-verify-req025-ac6.ts, deleted after use): a stubbed grammy Bot whose api.config.use transformer returns `{ok:false, error_code:429, parameters:{retry_after:1}}` on the first sendMessage call and a normal 200-shaped success on the second; `createRateLimitedSender(bot, DEFAULT_RATE_LIMITER_CONFIG).send(...)` resolved successfully after exactly 2 underlying API calls (1 failed-429, 1 succeeded), waited ~1005ms (>= the 1s retry_after) before the retry, and the caller's single `send()` promise resolved exactly once -- backoff-and-retry, not a dropped message, message ultimately delivered exactly once

issues.title: DrizzleQueryError wraps the underlying pg unique-violation error under `.cause` -- design's implicit assumption of a top-level `.code` needed a one-level unwrap
issues.description: REQ-025.md §3.1 step 4 describes catching a Postgres error code 23505 directly. In practice, drizzle-orm/node-postgres's insert throws a DrizzleQueryError whose OWN `.code` property is undefined -- the real pg driver error (carrying `.code === '23505'`) is nested one level down on `.cause`. This was caught live during AC1 verification (phase 2's first run returned `{kind:'failed', error:{...23505...}}` instead of `skipped-already-sent`, discovered by inspecting the actual error object in the outcome), and fixed in domain/notification.ts's `pgErrorCode()` helper, which checks the top-level `.code` first, then unwraps `.cause.code` as a fallback. Re-verified after the fix: phase 2 correctly returns skipped-already-sent. Filed as MINOR (not a design gap requiring rework) since the design's own step-4 language ('Postgres error code 23505') is correct about WHICH error to detect, just silent on drizzle-orm's specific wrapping shape -- an implementation-level detail, not a business-rule ambiguity.
issues.recommendation: No action needed -- already fixed and re-verified in this run. Noting for REVIEWER/future DATA-DESIGNER awareness that any other future direct-insert-based idempotency check against drizzle-orm/node-postgres should unwrap `.cause` the same way.

issues.title: scheduler/runner.ts's startScheduledJobs constructs its own internal logger rather than the design's stated 'via this codebase's existing log.ts logger' being wired through an explicit parameter
issues.description: REQ-025.md §7's stated signature is `startScheduledJobs(jobs: readonly ScheduledJobDefinition[]): SchedulerHandle` -- exactly one parameter -- while the same section's rule table says a failed run is 'caught and logged (via this codebase's existing log.ts logger)'. Implemented literally to the stated one-argument signature by having runner.ts construct its own logger via `createLogger('debug')` internally, relying on log.ts's LEVEL_ORDER making `.error()` calls fire regardless of which threshold is passed (error is the maximum severity level, so `LEVEL_ORDER['error'] < threshold` is never true for any valid LogLevel). This means index.ts's actual configured log level (from config.ts) is not honored for THIS module's error logs specifically -- they always print. No acceptance criterion tests log-level gating for scheduled-job failures (no concrete job even ships in this requirement, §7's own scope note -- startScheduledJobs([]) is called with an empty list), so this has no behavioral effect today, but is flagged in case REQ-026/027 (the first requirements to actually populate the job list) want the process-wide configured logger threaded through instead.
issues.recommendation: If REQ-026/027's own design wants the configured logLevel honored for job-failure logs, add a logger parameter to startScheduledJobs at that point (a design change, however small) rather than silently reusing this run's internal default.
